newsitem.title: USA: Quadrax to relinquish Wimbledon license.
newsitem.headline: Quadrax to relinquish Wimbledon license.

text.p: Quadrax Corp said on Monday that it relinquished the license to utilize the Wimbledon trademark in the United States for tennis rackets, because the arrangement is "not economically justified."

"Despite two years of effort, our experience is that the prestige associated with The All England Lawn and Tennis Club and the Wimbledon name never translated into any meaningful interest in Wimbledon branded tennis rackets," James Palermo, chairman and chief executive of Quadrax, said in a statement.
"As a result, maintaining the licensing arrangement is not economically justified," Palermo said.
The value of the licensing deal was described as in the "low six figures," Quadrax chief financial officer Edward Stoltenberg said. He could not be more specific about the value of the deal.

Quadrax has determined that its thermoplastic material is the differentiating feature in the tennis racket and it could market its tennis racquets to a larger base of retailers without the license, the company said.
The company had not marketed tennis racquets under any other name, Stoltenberg said.
Quadrax will continue to market its thermoplastic tennis racket through its own resource of outlets, or in conjunction with a major international partner, the company said.
Also, Quadrax said it can manufacture private label tennis rackets out of its patented material for other companies.
